package_info.package_manager: N/A (standalone Linux executable, not a package manager distribution)
package_info.why_malicious: The Maori ransomware is a malicious Linux executable that encrypts user files in the /home/<username> directory, appends a .maori extension, drops a ransom note, and deletes itself after execution. Its sole purpose is extortion via file encryption, with no legitimate functionality.

execution_context.file_location: Maori ransomware ELF binary (Go-compiled, executed on Linux)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code enumerates all files in the user's home directory, encrypts their entire contents, renames them with a .maori extension, and writes a ransom note into each affected directory.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Encrypting user files and demanding ransom is a classic ransomware behavior with no legitimate use case.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Linux executables do not recursively encrypt user files or drop ransom notes; such actions are highly anomalous.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup or archiving tools may read and write user files, but do not encrypt and rename them in this manner or demand ransom.
key_indicators: Bulk file encryption in user directories
Dropping ransom note (README_MAORI.txt) in each directory

execution_context.file_location: Maori ransomware ELF binary (Go-compiled, executed on Linux)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
// Pseudocode representation
self_delete() // deletes the executable after completion
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After encrypting files and dropping ransom notes, the code deletes its own executable from the victim machine to reduce forensic evidence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Self-deletion is a common anti-forensics technique used by malware to hinder analysis and detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not typically delete its own binary after execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate installers or updaters may self-delete after running, but not in the context of file encryption and extortion.

attack_chain.action: Enumerate and encrypt all user files in /home/<username>, appending .maori extension and dropping ransom notes.
attack_chain.leads_to: Files are rendered inaccessible to the user; ransom note is presented.

attack_chain.action: Delete the ransomware executable from the victim machine to remove evidence.
attack_chain.leads_to: Reduces forensic footprint and complicates incident response.

behavioral_signatures: Bulk file encryption in user home directories
Dropping README_MAORI.txt ransom note in multiple directories
Self-deletion of the malware binary after execution
file_indicators: Disappearance of suspicious ELF binary after file encryption
network_indicators: No explicit C2 or exfiltration observed; ransom note instructs to contact via Tox or onionmail
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for rapid, bulk file modifications and the creation of files with the .maori extension in user home directories. Alert on the appearance of README_MAORI.txt in multiple directories. Detect and quarantine unknown ELF binaries that disappear after execution. Use file integrity monitoring and endpoint detection to identify mass encryption and self-deleting binaries.
